items.title: Claude can now operate lab hardware
items.oneliner: Anthropic's hardware standard lets Claude run real instruments; QuEra recovered a quantum laser lock in 695 of 700 trials.

items.title: Tencent released a giant open model
items.oneliner: Tencent's 770B Hy4 preview ships with 1M-plus context, signaling China still bets on frontier-scale open models.

items.title: The EU AI Act gets real
items.oneliner: EU AI Act enforcement has started, so model makers should expect regulator questions before high-risk rules fully land.

items.title: Qubes fixed a dom0 code execution bug
items.oneliner: A compromised qube could reach Qubes dom0 through qvm-copy-to-vm error handling; isolation only works if plumbing does.

items.title: Europe revived its encryption backdoor push
items.oneliner: The EU's ProtectEU plan revives lawful-access backdoors, putting secure messaging and compliance architecture back on collision course.

items.title: OpenAI cut off Cursor's hosted models
items.oneliner: OpenAI is ending Cursor's model deal after the SpaceX acquisition, reminding every AI product team that platform risk is real.

items.title: Samsung showed a memory-heavy CXL accelerator
items.oneliner: Samsung and Xcena's MX1 packs 2TB DDR5 and 3,072 RISC-V cores, targeting memory-bound ML bottlenecks directly.

items.title: Amp introduced remote coding agents called orbs
items.oneliner: Amp's orbs turn remote coding agents into persistent, sleepable workspaces, pushing dev environments closer to cloud-native teammates.

items.title: CPython now officially supports RISC-V
items.oneliner: CPython added tier-3 RISC-V support, a small but real signal that open silicon is entering mainstream developer tooling.

items.title: South Korea is subsidizing AI access
items.oneliner: South Korea picked providers for free public AI access, turning national distribution into the next competitive moat.
